tldr: AWS and Anthropic introduced the Claude apps gateway on Jul 8, pitching it as a self-hosted control plane giving organizations a single point of control over access, cost, and policy for Claude Code and Claude Desktop.
whats_new: InfoQ's Jul 15 coverage confirms AWS shipped the gateway, centralizing identity, policy, telemetry, routing, and spend caps for Claude Code and Claude Desktop deployments.
why_it_matters: A self-hosted control plane gives platform teams centralized spend caps, policy, and telemetry for agentic coding tools instead of per-seat API keys — the governance layer most teams currently build in-house.

status.detail: Self-hosted control plane for Claude Code and Claude Desktop went from announcement to independently-confirmed shipping within a week.

beats.headline: AWS and Anthropic introduce the Claude apps gateway for AWS
beats.summary: A self-hosted control plane pitched as a single point of control over access, cost, and policy for Claude Code and Claude Desktop.

beats.headline: InfoQ confirms it shipped with identity, policy, telemetry, routing, and spend caps
beats.summary: Independent coverage a week later confirms the gateway is live and details its centralized controls.

open_questions: Does AWS publish standalone pricing for running the gateway, or is it bundled into existing Claude-on-AWS billing?
How does the gateway's spend-cap and policy model compare to Anthropic's own admin console for Claude Code?
take_for_builders: If you're running Claude Code or Claude Desktop at scale on AWS, evaluate the apps gateway now — it centralizes identity, policy, telemetry, routing, and spend caps instead of per-seat API keys.
